lines.text: The Fed cuts rates. Your mortgage payment? Still the same.
lines.caption: Rates down. Payment unchanged.

lines.text: For a standard U.S. fixed-rate mortgage, you signed a contract with a set interest rate.
lines.caption: Your rate is set in the contract.

lines.text: That rate does not reset when the Fed changes its overnight lending target.
lines.caption: Policy rate ≠ your contract rate.

lines.text: Your scheduled principal-and-interest payment stays flat, even if market rates fall.
lines.caption: Scheduled principal + interest stay flat.

lines.text: Refinancing replaces that old mortgage with a new loan. It is a separate decision,
lines.caption: Refinancing means a new loan.

lines.text: with approval, closing costs, and a new term to compare.
lines.caption: Compare approval, costs and term.

lines.text: One catch: taxes and insurance can still change your total monthly bill.
lines.caption: Taxes and insurance can change.

lines.text: A rate cut changes the backdrop. It does not rewrite your contract.
lines.caption: A rate cut does not rewrite your contract.
